open_points.subject: document acceptance
open_points.text: Accepted by the owner on 2026-11-18, with decisions R0-06 to R0-10.
open_points.question: Are R0-01 through R0-05 and P-01 through P-06 also accepted product decisions, or are only R0-06 through R0-10 accepted?
options: All R0 and P items are accepted
Only R0-06 through R0-10 are accepted
R0-01 through R0-05 and P-01 through P-06 have another status
open_points.default_guess: Treat every stated R0 and P item as accepted.

open_points.subject: open questions handoff
open_points.text: Questions OQ-05, OQ-07 and OQ-08 stay open.
open_points.question: Who must decide these questions, by what deadline or gate, and may implementation or delivery proceed before each is closed?
options: They must close before implementation
They may remain open during implementation but must close before production
Each has its own blocking gate
open_points.default_guess: Require all three to close before the first production delivery.

open_points.subject: prototype evidence
open_points.text: The prototype is evidence, not product code.
open_points.question: When the prose and prototype behavior differ, which one is authoritative, and which prototype behaviors beyond the explicitly accepted P-items are requirements?
options: The prose is authoritative and only P-items are requirements
Prototype behavior is authoritative evidence for every described claim
Differences must reopen the affected claim
open_points.default_guess: Treat the prose and accepted P-items as authoritative and reopen any discrepancy.

open_points.subject: delivery completion
open_points.text: brings progress photos of a renovation object from the object's Syncthing-fork folder on the VPS to the Client Portal's binary store, and hands back what is needed to publish each photo
open_points.question: What exact event constitutes a successful delivery: preparing and storing the binary, returning the reference and body, creating the hidden Portal record, recording that publication, or making the photo visible?
options: Placement in the binary store
Hidden Portal record plus publication mark
Visible client photo
Separate completion states for each step
open_points.default_guess: Model placement, hidden publication, recorded publication and visibility as separate completion states.

open_points.subject: client-visible state
open_points.text: A photo exists for the client only after it is published through the Portal's own operation.
open_points.question: Does "exists for the client" mean a hidden record exists in the client's cabinet or that the client can see it, given that publication is later said to create a record hidden from the client?
options: Publication creates a hidden cabinet record that the client cannot see
Publication makes the photo visible
Only the later show operation makes it exist for the client
open_points.default_guess: Publication creates a hidden record; only show makes it visible.

witness.initial: A photo has been placed but has no Portal record.
events: The calling flow publishes the placed photo through the Portal operation.
The client opens the cabinet before the owner shows the photo.
outcomes: The product statement can be read to say the photo now exists for the client.
R0-06 and Primary actions say the record is hidden and the client cannot see it.

open_points.subject: automatic delivery
open_points.text: The owner takes a photo on the phone and it can reach the client's cabinet without anyone copying files to the server by hand.
open_points.question: Which actor and concrete sequence move the photo after it reaches the synchronized folder, and does "can reach" promise an automatic workflow or only owner-initiated actions?
options: Owner starts one end-to-end flow
Owner separately scans, places, publishes and shows
A background process prepares it after synchronization
open_points.default_guess: The owner starts one end-to-end flow, with an explicit show step after review.

open_points.subject: object identity
open_points.text: connects an object to its folder
open_points.question: What identifies an object, and is an object exactly the same entity as a Registry project or Portal project?
options: Object identity is the Registry project id
Object and Registry project are distinct with an explicit mapping
Object identity is local to the deliverer
open_points.default_guess: Use the Registry project id as the object's canonical identity.

open_points.subject: owner initiation surface
open_points.text: A delivery starts from an action of the owner in the workplace.
open_points.question: What system or interface is "the workplace," how is the owner authenticated there, and which concrete action starts the calling flow?
options: A cabinet_kernel user interface
A command-line operation
Another workplace application
open_points.default_guess: A cabinet_kernel UI action authenticated as the owner.

open_points.subject: calling-flow authorization
open_points.text: It reaches the deliverer over an authenticated boundary.
open_points.question: What identity and authorization claims are bound to a request, and how does the deliverer ensure the caller may act on the supplied project id?
options: One service-wide bearer token may access every project
Per-owner or per-project authorization is checked
Network access plus a bearer token is sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Use a service identity restricted to the single owner and authorize every configured project.

open_points.subject: bearer-token lifecycle
open_points.text: authenticated by the deliverer's own bearer token
open_points.question: Who issues, stores, rotates and revokes this token, and what happens to in-flight or retried requests after rotation?
options: Static manually provisioned secret
Rotatable service credential with overlap
Short-lived issued token
open_points.default_guess: Use a rotatable service credential with a brief overlap period.

open_points.subject: source identifier
open_points.text: project id, source ids, Portal photo id
open_points.question: What is a source id, how is it generated, how long is it valid, and does it identify a path, one scan observation or immutable source content?
options: Content hash
Opaque scan-result id bound to content and project
Folder-relative path
Path plus file metadata
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque scan-result id bound to project, relative path and observed content hash.

open_points.subject: file reference
open_points.text: statuses, file reference, publication body
open_points.question: What is the schema and lifetime of the file reference, and how is it guaranteed not to reveal a server path or credential?
options: Opaque binary-store key
Portal-relative URL
Structured store namespace and object id
open_points.default_guess: Return an opaque store key in a documented namespace.

open_points.subject: publication body
open_points.text: statuses, file reference, publication body
open_points.question: What exact fields, types and invariants are in the publication body, and which values are authoritative when the Portal operation is called?
options: Complete Portal create-photo request
A partial payload the calling flow completes
An opaque signed payload
open_points.default_guess: Return a versioned complete Portal create-photo payload except for Portal-managed fields.

open_points.subject: scan status model
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed, published, settling, duplicate or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: What are the precise entry and exit conditions, precedence and allowed transitions for each status?
options: Exactly one mutually exclusive status with defined precedence
Several simultaneous flags rendered as one status
Status is recomputed on every scan
open_points.default_guess: Define one mutually exclusive, recomputed status with explicit precedence and transitions.

open_points.subject: duplicate status
open_points.text: duplicate
open_points.question: Duplicate of what—another path in the current folder, a placement in the same project, a placement in another project, or an already published Portal photo?
options: Same content within the same project
Same content anywhere in the deliverer
Same path appearing more than once
Already placed or published content
open_points.default_guess: Same source content already placed in the same project.

open_points.subject: rejection reasons
open_points.text: rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Which conditions are permanent rejection rather than settling or transient failure, and what stable reason codes are returned?
options: A closed enumeration of reason codes
Free-form diagnostic text
Transient and permanent errors are separate fields
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed, versioned set of reason codes and distinguish transient failures.

open_points.subject: unknown project refusal
open_points.text: unknown project, unconfirmed connection or unavailable folder is refused; nothing is changed
open_points.question: What observable response distinguishes these three refusals, and does an unavailable folder include missing paths, permission errors, mount failures and timeouts?
options: Distinct stable errors for each cause
One generic project-unavailable error
Only logs distinguish the causes
open_points.default_guess: Return distinct stable error codes without exposing server paths.

open_points.subject: placement batch semantics
open_points.text: a bad file is reported on its own and the others proceed
open_points.question: What happens when a non-file-specific failure occurs midway through a batch, and is the result an ordered per-source outcome, an atomic transaction or a resumable partial result?
options: Independent per-source commits and outcomes
Whole batch is atomic except validation failures
Stop on infrastructure failure and report committed items
open_points.default_guess: Commit independently per source, stop only affected work, and return an outcome for every requested source.

open_points.subject: changed-file detection
open_points.text: a file that changed since it was scanned is not placed
open_points.question: Which observed properties prove that the file is unchanged, and how is replacement during reading prevented from producing a mixed or stale image?
options: Rehash bytes immediately before and during placement
Compare size and modification time
Read a snapshot and verify the resulting hash against the scan
open_points.default_guess: Read one snapshot, hash it, and place only if that hash equals the scan-bound source id.

open_points.subject: idempotent placement
open_points.text: Place the same photo again | the first result, nothing written | none
open_points.question: Does the repeat still return the first result when the store object is missing, corrupted or inaccessible, and can authentication, project and infrastructure failures still occur?
options: Always replay the recorded first result
Verify the stored binary and fail if unavailable
Repair the stored binary idempotently
open_points.default_guess: Verify that the recorded store object exists and matches; report an infrastructure or integrity failure without silently rewriting it.

witness.initial: A placement record exists, but its prepared binary has been removed from the store.
events: The calling flow requests placement of the same source content again.
outcomes: "the first result" returns a reference to a missing binary with no failure.
An integrity-aware implementation refuses or repairs the placement.
witness.observer: The calling flow and, after publication, the owner

open_points.subject: Portal publication operation
open_points.text: Publish a placed photo (Portal operation, by the calling flow)
open_points.question: What exact Portal operation is called, what request fields come from the deliverer versus the flow, and how is the resulting Portal photo id obtained?
options: A specified synchronous create-photo endpoint
An asynchronous Portal workflow
A kernel-owned adapter whose contract is defined elsewhere
open_points.default_guess: Use a specified synchronous Portal create-photo operation returning the photo id.

open_points.subject: publication recovery
open_points.text: The calling flow records the Portal photo id at the deliverer right after publishing.
open_points.question: How is the system reconciled when Portal publication succeeds but recording the publication times out, fails or the calling flow crashes?
options: Retry record-publication idempotently with the same id
Query the Portal and reconcile manually or automatically
Hide the orphaned Portal record and republish
Accept an indefinitely placed-but-published orphan
open_points.default_guess: Retry the idempotent record call and provide an owner-visible reconciliation path.

witness.initial: The source is placed and has no publication mark.
events: The calling flow creates a hidden Portal photo successfully.
The flow loses the response or crashes before recording the Portal photo id.
outcomes: The implementation republishes and may create a second Portal record.
The implementation discovers or manually reconciles the first record and records its id.

open_points.subject: publication-id validation
open_points.text: which Portal photo a placed source became
open_points.question: How can the deliverer verify that the supplied Portal photo id actually refers to the placed binary and project when it never calls the Portal?
options: Trust the authenticated calling flow completely
Require a verifiable Portal receipt
Store the claim without verification and expose it as caller-attested
open_points.default_guess: Require a verifiable receipt or explicitly define the mark as a trusted caller assertion.

open_points.subject: first publication mark
open_points.text: a different photo id for the same source, is refused
open_points.question: What prevents the first supplied photo id from being wrong, and how is an erroneous first mark corrected?
options: No correction; first write is final
Owner-authorized correction with audit history
Verification makes an incorrect first mark impossible
open_points.default_guess: Allow an audited owner-authorized correction after verifying the Portal record.

open_points.subject: show operation
open_points.text: Show the photo (Portal operation, by the owner)
open_points.question: What exact Portal state change makes a hidden photo visible, and is visibility reversible through a hide operation?
options: Set a visibility flag and allow later hiding
Publish is a second irreversible transition
Portal-specific behavior outside this product contract
open_points.default_guess: The owner toggles Portal visibility, and may later hide the photo.

open_points.subject: hide operation
open_points.text: The earlier delivery stays in the Portal until the owner hides it.
open_points.question: Which promise or action carries hiding a wrong or superseded photo, and what observable result and failure does that action have?
options: Add a Portal hide action to the product workflow
Treat hiding as an explicitly external Portal capability
Do not support correction after showing
open_points.default_guess: Carry an explicit external Portal hide action with observable visibility state.

open_points.subject: evidence applicability
open_points.text: No run has used a live Syncthing folder, the kernel or the VPS.
open_points.question: Which claims remain unproven until those environments are exercised, and what gate prevents production use before that evidence exists?
options: Require live integration evidence before production
Accept prototype evidence as sufficient
Require only a VPS smoke test
open_points.default_guess: Require an end-to-end VPS run with a live synchronized test folder and kernel before production.

open_points.subject: supported image inputs
open_points.text: Image files in an object's folder
open_points.question: Which file formats, encodings, dimensions, animation modes and corruption cases count as supported image files?
options: A closed allowlist such as JPEG, PNG and HEIC
Any format the image library can decode
JPEG only for the first version
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed, versioned allowlist and reject everything else with stable reasons.

open_points.subject: folder traversal
open_points.text: Image files in an object's folder
open_points.question: Are subdirectories traversed, are symbolic links followed, and how are hard links, special files, hidden files and paths escaping the configured root handled?
options: Recursive regular files only, never follow links
Top-level regular files only
Follow configured subfolders and safe links
open_points.default_guess: Traverse only explicitly selected subfolders, accept regular files, and never follow links outside the root.

open_points.subject: source hash
open_points.text: source hash
open_points.question: Which hash algorithm and byte representation define source identity, and can that definition be migrated without changing photo identity?
options: SHA-256 of original file bytes
Hash of decoded pixels
Versioned hash scheme stored with each record
open_points.default_guess: Store a versioned SHA-256 hash of the complete original file bytes.

open_points.subject: placement record ownership
open_points.text: A record of each placement
open_points.question: How long are placement records and prepared images retained, and what happens when a project connection is removed, a Portal photo is hidden or the source file disappears?
options: Retain indefinitely
Retain while any Portal record refers to the binary
Owner-controlled cleanup with reference checks
open_points.default_guess: Retain while referenced by the Portal and provide audited owner-controlled cleanup only when unreferenced.

open_points.subject: binary-store consistency
open_points.text: The prepared images, which live in the Portal binary store.
open_points.question: What consistency and recovery rules apply if writing the binary succeeds but writing the placement record fails, or vice versa?
options: Transactional store and database commit
Write binary then reconcile orphaned objects
Write record then repair missing binaries
open_points.default_guess: Write the binary first, commit the record only after success, and garbage-collect verified orphaned binaries.

open_points.subject: connection management
open_points.text: One connection per object: its Registry project id, root folder, photo and invoice subfolders and the owner's confirmation.
open_points.question: What concrete action creates, confirms, changes, disables or removes a connection, what validates its paths and project id, and what are the observable results and failures?
options: Owner-managed deliverer operation
Static administrator configuration
Calling flow writes connections through a defined API
open_points.default_guess: Provide authenticated owner-managed create, confirm, update and disable operations with path containment validation.

open_points.subject: connection cardinality
open_points.text: One record per object, keyed by the Registry project id
open_points.question: Can one Registry project have multiple renovation objects or folder roots, and if so how can a record be both per object and keyed only by project id?
options: Exactly one object per Registry project
Multiple objects require a compound key
Object and project are synonyms
open_points.default_guess: Declare exactly one deliverer object per Registry project for the first version.

open_points.subject: invoice subfolder
open_points.text: photo and invoice subfolders
open_points.question: Why is an invoice subfolder stored when R0-03 excludes expense documents, and may the deliverer inspect or expose it?
options: Store it for shared connection data but never access it
Remove it from this service's data model
Support invoices despite R0-03
open_points.default_guess: Store it only if the shared connection model requires it, and explicitly prohibit this service from reading it.

open_points.subject: Registry interaction
open_points.text: The Client Portal API and Registry are not called by the deliverer.
open_points.question: Which actor obtains and validates the Registry project id used to create a connection, and what happens if the Registry project is later renamed, removed or inaccessible?
options: The calling flow resolves and validates it
The owner supplies an unverified id
A separate connection-management service owns synchronization
open_points.default_guess: The calling flow resolves it and the deliverer stores the immutable id as a trusted assertion.

open_points.subject: binary-store interface
open_points.text: Client Portal binary store
open_points.question: What storage system, namespace, write protocol, permissions and atomicity contract constitute the Portal binary store?
options: Shared filesystem with a defined directory contract
Object storage with an API
A Portal-owned storage adapter
open_points.default_guess: Use a Portal-owned storage adapter contract rather than relying on an undocumented filesystem layout.

open_points.subject: pixel-only privacy rule
open_points.text: Nothing but pixels may reach the store.
open_points.question: Which non-pixel data is permitted as necessary image-container structure, and must color profiles, thumbnails, filenames, ancillary chunks and all other metadata be removed?
options: Strip every optional metadata item and write a fresh encoded image
Only EXIF, GPS, XMP and comments are forbidden
Preserve color-management metadata but remove identifying metadata
open_points.default_guess: Decode and freshly encode pixels, preserving only explicitly approved non-identifying color information.

open_points.subject: Portal binary size
open_points.text: The Portal reads at most 26 214 400 bytes per binary.
open_points.question: Must every prepared image be guaranteed below this limit, and if an encoded image exceeds it, should quality or dimensions be reduced or should the source be rejected?
options: Iteratively reduce quality or dimensions to fit
Reject oversized prepared images
The 2000-pixel limit is assumed to guarantee the byte limit
open_points.default_guess: Guarantee the byte limit by bounded re-encoding, then reject if it still cannot be met.

open_points.subject: photo_date representation
open_points.text: The Portal stores `photo_date` as UTC without an offset
open_points.question: What exact string or database representation is required, and how is a timezone-less value distinguished from a genuinely UTC instant?
options: UTC instant serialized without a suffix
Naive datetime whose fields are UTC
Portal-specific formatted value
open_points.default_guess: Use a documented Portal-specific naive datetime whose fields are normalized to UTC.

open_points.subject: first production project
open_points.text: The first run against the production Portal uses that test project only.
open_points.question: What constitutes the first run, who authorizes expansion beyond Proyecto Demo Facebook, and what evidence or success criteria permit another project?
options: One successful end-to-end photo lifecycle
A fixed trial period
Explicit owner approval after documented checks
open_points.default_guess: Require a successful place, publish, record, show and hide cycle followed by explicit owner approval.

open_points.subject: service inactivity
open_points.text: The service delivers nothing by itself.
open_points.question: May it scan folders, compute statuses, clean orphaned data or retry interrupted work without an owner action, or is every read and write prohibited until a request?
options: No autonomous scanning or mutation
Background scanning is allowed but placement is not
Retries and maintenance may run autonomously
open_points.default_guess: Allow read-only indexing and safe retries, but no new placement or publication without owner initiation.

open_points.subject: content identity scope
open_points.text: A delivered photo is identified by its content.
open_points.question: Does content mean original file bytes or decoded visual pixels, and are metadata-only changes, re-encoding, rotation normalization or edits considered a new photo?
options: Exact original bytes
Decoded oriented pixel content
Prepared output bytes
open_points.default_guess: Use exact original file bytes for source identity, while separately recording prepared-output integrity.

witness.initial: A JPEG has already been delivered.
events: The phone or synchronization tool rewrites only its metadata without changing visible pixels.
The owner scans the folder again.
outcomes: A byte-hash implementation reports a new ready photo.
A pixel-hash implementation reports the existing photo as already placed.

open_points.subject: same content at multiple paths
open_points.text: One placement exists per project and source content
open_points.question: If identical content appears under two filenames or subfolders in one project, is there one selectable photo, two source entries sharing one placement, or one rejected duplicate?
options: One canonical source with duplicate aliases
Two source entries sharing one placement
One source is rejected as duplicate
open_points.default_guess: Show both paths as source entries, designate one canonical placement and mark the others duplicate.

open_points.subject: stability test
open_points.text: A file is taken only after it has been unchanged for two minutes
open_points.question: Which properties must remain unchanged, from which observation is the two-minute interval measured, and how are coarse timestamps, clock changes and writes preserving size or modification time handled?
options: Stable size and mtime for two minutes
Stable content hash across observations two minutes apart
Filesystem close notifications plus a two-minute delay
open_points.default_guess: Require matching size, mtime and content hash in observations at least two monotonic minutes apart.

open_points.subject: ignored paths
open_points.text: Syncthing's temporary files and the phone's trash are ignored.
open_points.question: Which exact names or path patterns identify temporary files and phone trash, and are matches case-sensitive or platform-specific?
options: A documented closed pattern list
Configuration per connection
Heuristics based on names
open_points.default_guess: Use a documented, tested and configurable pattern list with platform-specific case rules.

open_points.subject: camera date extraction
open_points.text: The photo date comes from the camera record
open_points.question: Which metadata fields count as the camera record, and what precedence applies when original, digitized and offset-bearing timestamps disagree?
options: DateTimeOriginal with its offset, then documented fallbacks
Earliest camera timestamp
Any parser-provided capture time
open_points.default_guess: Use DateTimeOriginal with OffsetTimeOriginal, followed by a documented field order.

open_points.subject: timezone conversion
open_points.text: otherwise from the file's modification time, and is delivered as UTC without an offset
open_points.question: Which timezone is used when the camera timestamp has no offset, and how are daylight-saving ambiguity and nonexistent local times resolved?
options: Configured timezone per object
Owner's current timezone
VPS timezone
Reject timestamps without an offset
open_points.default_guess: Require a configured timezone per object and flag ambiguous or nonexistent local times for owner confirmation.

witness.initial: A photo contains `2026-10-25 02:30:00` without an offset in a timezone where that local time occurs twice.
events: The deliverer extracts the camera date.
It converts the value to UTC.
outcomes: The implementation chooses the first occurrence and stores one UTC instant.
The implementation chooses the second occurrence and stores a UTC instant one hour later.
witness.observer: The owner and client viewing the photo date

open_points.subject: modification-time semantics
open_points.text: otherwise from the file's modification time
open_points.question: Does synchronization preserve the phone's original modification time reliably, and if it is missing, invalid or changed by copying, should the file be rejected or use another date?
options: Trust filesystem mtime
Reject when no trustworthy camera timestamp exists
Ask the owner to supply a date
open_points.default_guess: Use mtime but report its provenance and allow owner correction before publication.

open_points.subject: image preparation
open_points.text: is upright and is at most 2000 px on its longest side
open_points.question: What output format, color space, resize algorithm, quality, transparency handling and animation/frame policy produce the prepared image?
options: A fixed deterministic encoding profile
Preserve source format after metadata removal
Choose encoding dynamically by source type
open_points.default_guess: Define a deterministic sRGB encoding profile, flatten unsupported transparency, and reject animation unless a frame policy is explicitly chosen.

open_points.subject: delivery file scope
open_points.text: Everything under `foto`, or a chosen part?
open_points.question: Is the delivery source all eligible files recursively under `foto`, an owner-selected subtree, or individually selected files from a broader scan?
options: All eligible files under `foto`
Owner-configured subtrees
Owner selects individual files returned by a scan
open_points.default_guess: Scan all eligible files under `foto` and let the owner select individual files for placement.

open_points.subject: subfolder semantics
open_points.text: Do subfolders mean Portal sections
open_points.question: Do subfolders affect Portal placement, and if so how are nested paths mapped to section identifiers, renamed folders and files moved between folders?
options: Subfolders have no Portal meaning
First-level folders map to Portal sections
Full nested paths map to a section hierarchy
open_points.default_guess: Give subfolders no Portal meaning in the first version.

open_points.subject: caption source
open_points.text: where does a caption come from?
open_points.question: Are captions unsupported, entered by the owner, derived from filenames or sidecar data, and at which step may they be edited?
options: No captions in the first version
Owner enters a caption before publication
Caption comes from a sidecar file
Caption derives from the filename
open_points.default_guess: Allow an optional owner-entered caption before publication; never infer one from the filename.

open_points.subject: service deployment
open_points.text: Where does the service run
open_points.question: On which host, runtime and operating account does the service run, and how are its access to source folders and the Portal store isolated?
options: On the VPS as a dedicated service account
In a container on the VPS
On the owner's PC with mounted remote storage
open_points.default_guess: Run it on the VPS in an isolated container or dedicated account with read-only source access and narrowly scoped store write access.

open_points.subject: kernel connectivity
open_points.text: how does the kernel reach it?
open_points.question: What HTTPS endpoint, certificate trust, network exposure, authentication mechanism and retry/timeout contract connect the owner's PC to the service?
options: Public HTTPS endpoint with bearer authentication
Private VPN endpoint
Reverse tunnel from the VPS
open_points.default_guess: Use a private VPN endpoint with TLS and a rotatable bearer credential.

open_points.subject: legacy-date repair owner
open_points.text: Who repairs the old photo dates before the first delivery?
open_points.question: Which actor performs the repair, using what Portal operation, and who verifies that it succeeded?
options: Portal administrator repairs them
Owner repairs them through a Portal tool
A migration script owned by the Portal team repairs them
open_points.default_guess: Assign a Portal-owned migration run by its administrator and verified by the owner.

open_points.subject: legacy-date delivery gate
open_points.text: it must be settled for each project before delivery starts
open_points.question: How does the calling flow or deliverer know that a project's old dates are repaired, and what exact behavior blocks delivery when they are not?
options: A persisted per-project readiness flag
The owner confirms readiness manually
The Portal exposes a validation result
No technical gate; it is an operating procedure
open_points.default_guess: Require an owner-confirmed, audited readiness flag on the project connection and refuse scanning or placement until it is set.

open_points.subject: legacy-date failure scope
open_points.text: A project holding dates stored with an offset breaks on its first delivered photo
open_points.question: What does "breaks" observably mean, which operation fails or corrupts data, and can the system detect affected projects without attempting a delivery?
options: Portal publication fails
Existing dates are misparsed or rewritten
The photo list fails to load
A preflight check can identify affected records
open_points.default_guess: Define and run a non-mutating Portal preflight check before enabling the project.
